paper.title: Continuity of Regularized Channel Rényi Divergences
paper.snapshot_relation: Retained development source snapshot; not asserted byte-identical to published arXiv source.

comparisons.details: For all pairs of CPTP channels on common nonzero finite-dimensional complex input and output spaces, the punctured two-sided order-one limit of regularized sandwiched Renyi divergence equals regularized relative entropy. Input and output dimensions may differ. No support or finiteness premise; infinite target included.

Normalized positive density operators, base-two logarithms, inverse powers acting on support, explicit support-mismatch infinity above one and for relative entropy, and zero-quasi-entropy infinity below one.

Both explicitly optimize over pure unit-vector inputs with a reference isomorphic to the input space. Lean uses N tensor id; the paper uses id tensor N. Canonical input/output unitary swaps and simultaneous unitary invariance of both state divergences explain the difference. No new Lean equivalence theorem is supplied here.
EReal.toENNReal preserves infinity and clips negative values, but source nonnegativity propositions for relative entropy and p>=1/2, p!=1 show clipping changes no relevant state divergence.

Paper excludes p=1. Lean totalizes stateRenyi and regularizedRenyi at p=1 to zero; the punctured limit excludes this value. All orders sufficiently close to one are above one half. This totalization observation was obtained by definition interpretation, not a separately checked Lean theorem.
Lean recursive powers include a terminal one-dimensional factor and a specified association. Each block uses a reference of dimension (dim input)^n; entanglement across all uses is allowed.

Supremum over positive block lengths is the formal definition; the separate block-limit theorem identifies it with the normalized sequence limit for fixed p>=1/2 and p!=1, including p=1/2 and infinity. The zero-block value is immaterial at natural-number atTop.
Separate theorem identifies the positive-block supremum with the normalized relative-entropy block limit, including infinity. No finiteness or support assumption is added.

The restriction suffices for the order-one theorem but does not formalize all of the paper lemma at p>2. Exact block scaling supplies n-block normalization. Mapping accurately records this restriction.
